content: Oropharyngeal Anthrax The preferred treatment regimen for oropharyngeal anthrax includes Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV every 8 hours, combined with either Clindamycin 900 mg IV every 8 hours or Linezolid 600 mg IV every 12 hours. Alternative regimens may include one of the following: Levofloxacin 750 mg IV every 24 hours, Moxifloxacin 400 mg IV every 24 hours, Meropenem 2 g IV every 8 hours, Imipenem 1 g IV every 6 hours, Doripenem 500 mg IV every 8 hours, Vancomycin 60 mg/kg/day IV divided every 8 hours, Ampicillin 3 g IV every 6 hours, or Penicillin G 4 million units IV every 4 hours, combined with either Doxycycline 200 mg IV initially, then 100 mg IV every 12 hours, or Rifampin 600 mg IV every 8 hours. Treatment duration is 14 days or until the patient is clinically stable. For patients exposed to aerosolized spores, therapy should continue for 60 days, transitioning to oral therapy after the first 2 weeks. Ampicillin and Penicillin G are only recommended for penicillin-susceptible strains. If Vancomycin is used, maintain serum trough concentrations between 15–20 mcg/mL. Avoid Doxycycline in pregnant or lactating women and children under 8 years of age. Buccal Cellulitis The preferred empiric antimicrobial therapy includes Cefuroxime 50 mg/kg IV every 8 hours, or Cefuroxime 10–15 mg/kg PO every 12 hours (maximum dose: 1 g/day), or Ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg IV every 24 hours. An alternative regimen is Amoxicillin-Clavulanate 90 mg/kg/day PO divided every 12 hours. If meningitis is suspected, increase the Cefuroxime dose to 80 mg/kg IV every 8 hours or the Ceftriaxone dose to 50 mg/kg IV every 24 hours. Cervico-Facial Actinomycosis The preferred regimen involves Ampicillin 50 mg/kg/day IV every 8 hours for 4–6 weeks, followed by Penicillin V 2–4 g/day PO every 6 hours for 3–6 months. An alternative regimen includes Penicillin G 10–20 million units/day IV every 6 hours for 4–6 weeks, followed by Penicillin V 2–4 g/day PO every 6 hours for 3–6 months. For patients allergic to penicillin, consider Doxycycline, Clindamycin, or Erythromycin. Deep Neck Infections Necrotizing Fasciitis The preferred regimen includes Ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 8 hours, Clindamycin 600–900 mg IV every 8 hours, and Metronidazole 500 mg IV every 6 hours. Alternative regimens include Ampicillin-Sulbactam 2 g IV every 4 hours or Clindamycin 600 mg IV every 6 hours. For immunocompromised hosts, options include Cefotaxime 2 g IV every 6 hours, Ceftizoxime 4 g IV every 8 hours, Piperacillin 3 g IV every 4 hours, or Imipenem 500 mg IV every 6 hours. Facial Erysipelas Common causative pathogens include Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus spp. (Groups A, B, C, and G), Enterobacteriaceae, and Clostridium spp.. The preferred empiric therapy is Vancomycin 1 g IV every 12 hours. Alternative regimens include Daptomycin 4 mg/kg IV every 24 hours or Linezolid 600 mg IV every 12 hours. Mastoiditis For patients without recent antibiotic use, the preferred regimen is Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg/day PO every 6 hours. For patients with recent antibiotic use, options include Amoxicillin-Clavulanate 90 mg/kg/day PO every 12 hours, Cefdinir 14 mg/kg PO every 24 hours, Cefpodoxime 10 mg/kg/day PO every 12 hours (maximum dose: 400 mg/day), Cefprozil 30 mg/kg/day PO every 12 hours (maximum dose: 1 g/day), or Cefuroxime 15 mg/kg/day PO every 12 hours (maximum dose: 1 g/day). Treatment duration is 10 days for children under 2 years old and 5–7 days for children aged 2 years or older. Odontogenic Infections The preferred regimen is Clindamycin 300–450 mg PO every 6 hours or Clindamycin 600 mg IV every 6–8 hours. Alternative regimens include Amoxicillin-Clavulanic acid 875/125 mg PO every 12 hours, Amoxicillin-Clavulanic acid 500/125 mg PO every 8 hours, or Cefotetan 2 g IV every 12 hours. Orbital Cellulitis Common pathogens include Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and Staphylococcus aureus. Treat uncomplicated disease for 7–14 days. For moderate-to-severe disease, Fluconazole is recommended, while mild disease may be treated with topical Clotrimazole or Nystatin. Otitis Externa Common pathogens include Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Candida spp., Enterobacteriaceae, and Proteus spp.. Preferred therapy includes Neomycin, Polymyxin B, and Hydrocortisone topical application every 6–8 hours, along with Selenium Sulfide Shampoo for seborrhea-associated cases. Acute Otitis Media Common pathogens include Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and polymicrobial or viral agents. The preferred regimen is Amoxicillin 80–90 mg/kg/day PO divided every 12 hours. Alternative regimens include Cefdinir 14 mg/kg/day PO every 12 or 24 hours, Cefuroxime 30 mg/kg/day PO every 12 hours, or Ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg/day IM or IV every 24 hours. Reassess treatment response after 2–3 days.
